exploration.title: Spring Force
exploration.summary: Compare spring stretch with the force pulling it back.
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.question: How does doubling the stretch change an ideal spring’s restoring force?
exploration.explanation: A stretched spring pulls toward its resting length. This model reports the size of that restoring force, not its direction. With stiffness fixed at 20 N/m, each extra 0.01 m of stretch adds 0.20 N. The chosen stiffness describes an illustrative ideal spring. Real springs follow this relationship only within their elastic range; this is not a safe-load calculator.

experiments.title: Double the stretch
experiments.instruction: Predict whether doubling stretch doubles the force. Set Stretch to 0.05 m, record the force, then set 0.10 m. The stiffness stays fixed.
experiments.observe: Compare the two forces. What happened to their ratio, and how does that support or challenge your prediction?

experiments.title: Equal steps, equal changes
experiments.instruction: Predict what equal increases in stretch will do to force. Compare Stretch at 0.02 m, 0.04 m and 0.06 m. Keep the same ideal spring.
experiments.observe: Calculate the force increase between each pair. Explain why equal stretch steps produce equal force steps; then test the zero-stretch boundary.

exploration.misconception: A larger restoring force does not mean the spring pushes farther away. Its force acts back toward the resting length; the output shows magnitude only.
